NKJV.1: And Moses called all Israel, and said to them: “Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments which I speak in your hearing today, that you may learn them and be careful to observe them.
NKJV.2: The LORD our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.
NKJV.3: The LORD did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, those who are here today, all of us who are alive.
NKJV.4: The LORD talked with you face to face on the mountain from the midst of the fire.
NKJV.5: I stood between the LORD and you at that time, to declare to you the word of the LORD; for you were afraid because of the fire, and you did not go up the mountain. He said:
NKJV.6: ‘I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
NKJV.7: ‘You shall have no other gods before Me.
NKJV.8: ‘You shall not make for yourself a carved image—any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth;
NKJV.9: you shall not bow down to them nor serve them. For I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
NKJV.10: but showing mercy to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments.
NKJV.11: ‘You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not hold him guiltless who takes His name in vain.
NKJV.12: ‘Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.
NKJV.13: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
NKJV.14: but the seventh day is the Sabbath of the LORD your God. In it you shall do no work: you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your cattle, nor your stranger who is within your gates, that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you.
NKJV.15: And remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm; therefore the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
NKJV.16: ‘Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, that your days may be long, and that it may be well with you in the land which the LORD your God is giving you.
NKJV.20: ‘You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
NKJV.21: ‘You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife; and you shall not desire your neighbor’s house, his field, his male servant, his female servant, his ox, his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor’s.’
NKJV.22: “These words the LORD spoke to all your assembly, in the mountain from the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a loud voice; and He added no more. And He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
NKJV.23: “So it was, when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, that you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders.
NKJV.24: And you said: ‘Surely the LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice from the midst of the fire. We have seen this day that God speaks with man; yet he still lives.
NKJV.25: Now therefore, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us; if we hear the voice of the LORD our God anymore, then we shall die.
NKJV.26: For who is there of all flesh who has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived?
NKJV.27: You go near and hear all that the LORD our God may say, and tell us all that the LORD our God says to you, and we will hear and do it.’
NKJV.28: “Then the LORD heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me: ‘I have heard the voice of the words of this people which they have spoken to you. They are right in all that they have spoken.
NKJV.29: Oh, that they had such a heart in them that they would fear Me and always keep all My commandments, that it might be well with them and with their children forever!
NKJV.30: Go and say to them, “Return to your tents.”
NKJV.31: But as for you, stand here by Me, and I will speak to you all the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments which you shall teach them, that they may observe them in the land which I am giving them to possess.’
NKJV.32: “Therefore you shall be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
NKJV.33: You shall walk in all the ways which the LORD your God has commanded you, that you may live and that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days in the land which you shall possess.

ESV.1: And Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “Hear, O Israel, the statutes and the rules that I speak in your hearing today, and you shall learn them and be careful to do them.
ESV.2: The LORD our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.
ESV.3: Not with our fathers did the LORD make this covenant, but with us, who are all of us here alive today.
ESV.4: The LORD spoke with you face to face at the mountain, out of the midst of the fire,
ESV.5: while I stood between the LORD and you at that time, to declare to you the word of the LORD. For you were afraid because of the fire, and you did not go up into the mountain. He said:
ESV.6: “‘I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
ESV.7: “‘You shall have no other gods before  me.
ESV.8: “‘You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.
ESV.9: You shall not bow down to them or serve them; for I the LORD your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
ESV.10: but showing steadfast love to thousands  of those who love me and keep my commandments.
ESV.11: “‘You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain.
ESV.12: “‘Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.
ESV.13: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
ESV.14: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall not do any work, you or your son or your daughter or your male servant or your female servant, or your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates, that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you.
ESV.15: You shall remember that you were a slave  in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
ESV.16: “‘Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, that your days may be long, and that it may go well with you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
ESV.20: “‘And you shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
ESV.21: “‘And you shall not covet your neighbor's wife. And you shall not desire your neighbor's house, his field, or his male servant, or his female servant, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.’
ESV.22: “These words the LORD spoke to all your assembly at the mountain out of the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a loud voice; and he added no more. And he wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
ESV.23: And as soon as you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes, and your elders.
ESV.24: And you said, ‘Behold, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire. This day we have seen God speak with man, and man still live.
ESV.25: Now therefore why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God any more, we shall die.
ESV.26: For who is there of all flesh, that has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of fire as we have, and has still lived?
ESV.27: Go near and hear all that the LORD our God will say, and speak to us all that the LORD our God will speak to you, and we will hear and do it.’
ESV.28: “And the LORD heard your words, when you spoke to me. And the LORD said to me, ‘I have heard the words of this people, which they have spoken to you. They are right in all that they have spoken.
ESV.29: Oh that they had such a heart as this always, to fear me and to keep all my commandments, that it might go well with them and with their descendants  forever!
ESV.30: Go and say to them, “Return to your tents.”
ESV.31: But you, stand here by me, and I will tell you the whole commandment and the statutes and the rules that you shall teach them, that they may do them in the land that I am giving them to possess.’
ESV.32: You shall be careful therefore to do as the LORD your God has commanded you. You shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
ESV.33: You shall walk in all the way that the LORD your God has commanded you, that you may live, and that it may go well with you, and that you may live long in the land that you shall possess.

NASB.1: Then Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: 'Hear, O Israel, the statutes and the ordinances which I am speaking today in your hearing, that you may learn them and observe them carefully.
NASB.2: 'The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
NASB.3: 'The LORD did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, [with] all those of us alive here today.
NASB.4: 'The LORD spoke to you face to face at the mountain from the midst of the fire,
NASB.5: [while] I was standing between the LORD and you at that time, to declare to you the word of the LORD; for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said,
NASB.6: 'I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
NASB.7: 'You shall have no other gods before Me.
NASB.8: 'You shall not make for yourself an idol, [or] any likeness [of] what is in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the water under the earth.
NASB.9: 'You shall not worship them or serve them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the third and the fourth [generations] of those who hate Me,
NASB.10: but showing lovingkindness to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments.
NASB.11: 'You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave him unpunished who takes His name in vain.
NASB.12: 'Observe the sabbath day to keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.
NASB.13: 'Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
NASB.14: but the seventh day is a sabbath of the LORD your God; [in it] you shall not do any work, you or your son or your daughter or your male servant or your female servant or your ox or your donkey or any of your cattle or your sojourner who stays with you, so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you.
NASB.15: 'You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm; therefore the LORD your God commanded you to observe the sabbath day.
NASB.16: 'Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, that your days may be prolonged and that it may go well with you on the land which the LORD your God gives you.
NASB.20: 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
NASB.21: 'You shall not covet your neighbor's wife, and you shall not desire your neighbor's house, his field or his male servant or his female servant, his ox or his donkey or anything that belongs to your neighbor.'
NASB.22: 'These words the LORD spoke to all your assembly at the mountain from the midst of the fire, [of] the cloud and [of] the thick gloom, with a great voice, and He added no more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
NASB.23: 'And when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders.
NASB.24: 'You said, 'Behold, the LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice from the midst of the fire; we have seen today that God speaks with man, yet he lives.
NASB.25: 'Now then why should we die? For this great fire will consume us; if we hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer, then we will die.
NASB.26: 'For who is there of all flesh who has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire, as we [have], and lived?
NASB.27: 'Go near and hear all that the LORD our God says; then speak to us all that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do [it].'
NASB.28: 'The LORD heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard the voice of the words of this people which they have spoken to you. They have done well in all that they have spoken.
NASB.29: 'Oh that they had such a heart in them, that they would fear Me and keep all My commandments always, that it may be well with them and with their sons forever!
NASB.30: 'Go, say to them, 'Return to your tents.'
NASB.31: 'But as for you, stand here by Me, that I may speak to you all the commandments and the statutes and the judgments which you shall teach them, that they may observe [them] in the land which I give them to possess.'
NASB.32: 'So you shall observe to do just as the LORD your God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.
NASB.33: 'You shall walk in all the way which the LORD your God has commanded you, that you may live and that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong [your] days in the land which you will possess.

NLT.1: Moses called all the people of Israel together and said, “Listen carefully, Israel. Hear the decrees and regulations I am giving you today, so you may learn them and obey them!
NLT.2: “The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Mount Sinai.
NLT.3: The LORD did not make this covenant with our ancestors, but with all of us who are alive today.
NLT.4: At the mountain the LORD spoke to you face to face from the heart of the fire.
NLT.5: I stood as an intermediary between you and the LORD, for you were afraid of the fire and did not want to approach the mountain. He spoke to me, and I passed his words on to you. This is what he said:
NLT.6: “I am the LORD your God, who rescued you from the land of Egypt, the place of your slavery.
NLT.7: “You must not have any other god but me.
NLT.8: “You must not make for yourself an idol of any kind, or an image of anything in the heavens or on the earth or in the sea.
NLT.9: You must not bow down to them or worship them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God who will not tolerate your affection for any other gods. I lay the sins of the parents upon their children; the entire family is affected — even children in the third and fourth generations of those who reject me.
NLT.10: But I lavish unfailing love for a thousand generations on those who love me and obey my commands.
NLT.11: “You must not misuse the name of the LORD your God. The LORD will not let you go unpunished if you misuse his name.
NLT.12: “Observe the Sabbath day by keeping it holy, as the LORD your God has commanded you.
NLT.13: You have six days each week for your ordinary work,
NLT.14: but the seventh day is a Sabbath day of rest dedicated to the LORD your God. On that day no one in your household may do any work. This includes you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, your oxen and donkeys and other livestock, and any foreigners living among you. All your male and female servants must rest as you do.
NLT.15: Remember that you were once slaves in Egypt, but the LORD your God brought you out with his strong hand and powerful arm. That is why the LORD your God has commanded you to rest on the Sabbath day.
NLT.16: “Honor your father and mother, as the LORD your God commanded you. Then you will live a long, full life in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
NLT.20: “You must not testify falsely against your neighbor.
NLT.21: “You must not covet your neighbor’s wife. You must not covet your neighbor’s house or land, male or female servant, ox or donkey, or anything else that belongs to your neighbor.

AMP.1:
Then Moses summoned all Israel and said to them:
"Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments (legal decisions) which I am speaking today in your hearing, so that you may learn them and observe them carefully.
AMP.2: The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
AMP.3: The LORD did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, all of us who are alive here today.
AMP.4: The LORD spoke with you face to face at the mountain from the midst of the fire.
AMP.5: I was standing between the LORD and you at that time, to declare to you the word of the LORD; for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said,
AMP.6: 'I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
AMP.7: 'You shall have no other gods before Me.
AMP.8: 'You shall not make for yourself an idol [as an object to worship], or any likeness (form, manifestation) of what is in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the water under the earth.
AMP.9: You shall not worship them or serve them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous (impassioned) God [demanding what is rightfully and uniquely mine], visiting (avenging) the iniquity (sin, guilt) of the fathers on the children [that is, calling the children to account for the sins of their fathers], to the third and the fourth generations of those who hate Me,
AMP.10: but showing graciousness and lovingkindness to thousands [of generations] of those who love Me and keep My commandments.
AMP.11: 'You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain [that is, irreverently, in false affirmations or in ways that impugn the character of God]; for the LORD will not hold guiltless nor leave unpunished the one who takes His name in vain [disregarding its reverence and its power].
AMP.12: 'Observe the Sabbath day to keep it holy (set apart, dedicated to God), as the LORD your God commanded you.
AMP.13: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
AMP.14: but the seventh day is a Sabbath [a day of rest dedicated] to the LORD your God; on that day you shall not do any work, you or your son or your daughter or your male servant or your female servant or your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock or the stranger who stays inside your [city] gates, so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you.
AMP.15: You shall remember [with thoughtful concern] that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm; therefore the LORD your God has commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
AMP.16: 'Honor (respect, obey, care for) your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days [on the earth] may be prolonged and so that it may go well with you in the land which the LORD your God gives you.
AMP.20: 'You shall not give false testimony [that is, lie, withhold, or manipulate the truth] against your neighbor (any person).
AMP.21: 'You shall not covet [that is, desire and seek to acquire] your neighbor's wife, nor desire your neighbor's house, his field, his male servant or his female servant, his ox or his donkey or anything that belongs to your neighbor.'
AMP.22: "The LORD spoke these words with a great voice to all your assembly at the mountain out of the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, and He added no more. He wrote these commandments on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
AMP.23: And when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you approached me, all the leaders (heads) of your tribes and your elders;
AMP.24: and you said, 'Behold, the LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice from the midst of the fire; we have seen today that God speaks with man, yet he [still] lives.
AMP.25: Now then why should we die? For this great fire will consume us; if we hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer, then we will die.
AMP.26: For who is there of all flesh (mankind) who has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived?
AMP.27: You, Moses, go near and listen to everything that the LORD our God says; then speak to us everything that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will listen and do it.'
AMP.28: "The LORD heard your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard the words of this people which they have spoken to you. They have done well in all that they have spoken.
AMP.29: Oh that they had such a heart in them, that they would fear [and worship Me with awe-filled reverence and profound respect] and keep all My commandments always, so that it may go well with them and with their children forever!
AMP.30: Go and say to them, "Return to your tents."
AMP.31: But as for you, stand here by Me, and I will tell you all the commandments and the statutes and the judgments which you shall teach them, so that they may obey them in the land which I give them to possess.'
AMP.32: Therefore you shall pay attention and be careful to do just as the LORD your God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left [deviating from My commandments].
AMP.33: You shall walk [that is, live each and every day] in all the ways which the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live and so that it may be well with you, and that you may live long in the land which you will possess.

NIV.6: “I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.
NIV.7: “You shall have no other gods before me.
NIV.8: “You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the waters below.
NIV.9: You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sin of the fathers to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
NIV.10: but showing love to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.
NIV.11: “You shall not misuse the name of the Lord your God, for the Lord will not hold anyone guiltless who misuses his name.
NIV.12: “Observe the Sabbath day by keeping it holy, as the Lord your God has commanded you.
NIV.13: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
NIV.14: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any work, neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant, nor your ox, your donkey or any of your animals, nor the alien within your gates, so that your manservant and maidservant may rest, as you do.
NIV.15: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that the Lord your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore the Lord your God has commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
NIV.16: “Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God has commanded you, so that you may live long and that it may go well with you in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
NIV.20: “You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
NIV.21: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife. You shall not set your desire on your neighbor’s house or land, his manservant or maidservant, his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”
NIV.22: These are the commandments the Lord proclaimed in a loud voice to your whole assembly there on the mountain from out of the fire, the cloud and the deep darkness; and he added nothing more. Then he wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
NIV.23: When you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was ablaze with fire, all the leading men of your tribes and your elders came to me.
NIV.24: And you said, “The Lord our God has shown us his glory and his majesty, and we have heard his voice from the fire. Today we have seen that a man can live even if God speaks with him.
NIV.25: But now, why should we die? This great fire will consume us, and we will die if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any longer.
NIV.26: For what mortal man has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking out of fire, as we have, and survived?
NIV.27: Go near and listen to all that the Lord our God says. Then tell us whatever the Lord our God tells you. We will listen and obey.”
NIV.28: The Lord heard you when you spoke to me and the Lord said to me, “I have heard what this people said to you. Everything they said was good.
NIV.29: Oh, that their hearts would be inclined to fear me and keep all my commands always, so that it might go well with them and their children forever!
NIV.30: “Go, tell them to return to their tents.
NIV.31: But you stay here with me so that I may give you all the commands, decrees and laws you are to teach them to follow in the land I am giving them to possess.”
NIV.32: So be careful to do what the Lord your God has commanded you; do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
NIV.33: Walk in all the way that the Lord your God has commanded you, so that you may live and prosper and prolong your days in the land that you will possess.
